correctness.rationale: The recurrence gives D=6B−A and the shift-invariant AD−B²=8; consecutive coprimality and the period (1,3,17,3) modulo 48 imply pairwise coprimality and M≡17 mod 48 for n≥2 even. Then 25M+7 is divisible by 48, and the parity adjustment by odd M gives even k=K+2Mu with 48k≡7 mod M. For ℓ=2 or ℓ|B all forms are 1; for ℓ|M (necessarily ℓ≥5), exactly one of A,D is zero and the other equals 6B mod ℓ. The three residues are 1,−1/6,−6 using B²≡−8 and k≡7/48. All other primes are ≥5 and at most three residues of u are forbidden. For prime values, division of the reduced product expansion by a=Bk leaves the bracket j+k+ajk for the other two sequence terms j,k. It is a multiple of B for the middle modulus and vanishes modulo A,D by B(7−48k(u)), so the three distinct odd primes satisfy Korselt. Dickson is used only for infinitude at each fixed even n; strictly increasing forms give distinct products. The frozen verifier was inspected, not run. A separately written bounded check enumerated even K from 0 to 2AD−2 for n=2, found K=14918, and at u=363 recovered the three stated factors; exhaustive trial division to the respective integer square roots found each prime and the three Korselt remainders were exactly zero. This confirms the example only.

value.rationale: The progressions come from the known necessary compatibility conditions, not an arbitrary slice. Showing a fixed-divisor obstruction never defeats Dickson's conjecture in any positive even-index family is a concrete advance from candidate parametrization to conditional realization, despite using elementary local arithmetic. It is neither an unconditional prime-tuple theorem nor a new general Carmichael construction technique.
